# Obsidian Knowledge Graph Source

Source snapshot: `obsidian.json`.

## Entities

Vault, Note, Property, Tag, Internal Link, Backlink, Attachment, Template,
Canvas, Base, Core Plugin, Community Plugin, Obsidian Sync, Obsidian Publish.

## Topics

Vaults; files and folders; attachments; basic and advanced formatting; callouts;
internal links; aliases; embeds; properties; tags; command palette; hotkeys;
search; quick switcher; backlinks; outgoing links; graph view; daily notes;
templates; bookmarks; canvas; bases; file recovery; note composer; outline;
page preview; slash commands; slides; unique note creator; workspaces; random
note; sync; publish; community plugins; CSS snippets; Obsidian URI; backups;
import; and web viewer.

## Workflows

Create or open a vault; link notes; use Daily Notes with Templates.

## Graph Interpretation

Obsidian emphasizes Markdown files in a vault, explicit links, backlinks,
properties, tags, plugins, and local file operations. These are alternative
reference patterns and do not replace the application's generic object model.

coverage.note: The research identified the official Obsidian Help site and official documentation repository, but the completed research pass did not materialize every English Help page individually. This artifact therefore preserves the high-confidence structured topics extracted during the run without falsely claiming a complete page-for-page mirror.

schema_notes.llm_chunking_guidance: Use each topic as a primary retrieval object; derive semantic chunks from summary, facts, examples, commands, settings, limitations and relationships instead of fixed-size character windows.

topics.title: Create and manage a vault
topics.summary: A vault is the folder that Obsidian uses as the root of a note collection. Creating or opening a vault determines which folder Obsidian treats as the current knowledge workspace.

examples.scenario: Separate work and personal knowledge bases
examples.guidance: Use separate vault folders when you explicitly want separate Obsidian environments rather than only different folders inside one vault.

topics.title: Files and folders
topics.summary: Obsidian notes are primarily Markdown files stored in ordinary folders. Renaming and moving files can interact with internal links, so file and link-management behavior matters.

topics.title: Attachments
topics.summary: Obsidian can store non-Markdown files such as images and other attachments alongside notes. Attachment-location settings control where newly added files are placed.
settings: Settings → Files and links → Default location for new attachments

topics.title: Basic formatting syntax
topics.summary: Obsidian uses Markdown for headings, emphasis, lists, links, quotations, code and other common note structures.

topics.title: Advanced formatting
topics.summary: Advanced formatting extends basic Markdown with richer constructs for specialized technical and presentational content.

examples.purpose: Represent inline mathematical notation where supported.

topics.title: Callouts
topics.summary: Callouts are visually distinct blocks for notes, warnings, examples, tips and similar highlighted information represented using Markdown-style syntax.

topics.title: Internal links
topics.summary: Internal links connect vault content and can target whole notes, headings or blocks. They underpin navigation, backlinks and graph relationships.

topics.title: Aliases
topics.summary: Aliases let a note be referred to by alternate names while preserving a single underlying note identity.

topics.title: Embed files
topics.summary: Embeds transclude supported vault content into another note instead of only creating a navigational link.

topics.title: Properties
topics.summary: Properties attach structured metadata to notes and support values such as dates, numbers, tags, links or text.

examples.purpose: Represent a simple property in YAML-style frontmatter.

topics.title: Tags
topics.summary: Tags provide lightweight categorical labels for content and can use nested naming conventions.

topics.title: Command palette
topics.summary: The Command palette provides searchable access to commands exposed by Obsidian and enabled plugins.

topics.title: Hotkeys
topics.summary: Hotkeys map keyboard shortcuts to commands and are configured in Obsidian settings.

topics.title: Search
topics.summary: Search retrieves vault content and supports structured queries and filters beyond plain free-text matching.

topics.title: Quick switcher
topics.summary: Quick switcher is optimized for rapidly locating and opening notes from the keyboard.

topics.title: Backlinks
topics.summary: Backlinks expose inbound references by showing where the active note is referenced elsewhere in the vault.

topics.title: Outgoing links
topics.summary: Outgoing Links provides a view of references originating in the active note and complements Backlinks.

topics.title: Graph view
topics.summary: Graph view visualizes notes and the link relationships between them, with global and local graph workflows.

topics.title: Daily notes
topics.summary: Daily Notes creates or opens date-associated notes according to configurable date, folder and template conventions.

topics.title: Templates
topics.summary: The core Templates plugin inserts reusable note content from a configured templates folder and supports built-in template variables.

topics.title: Bookmarks
topics.summary: Bookmarks provide persistent shortcuts to frequently used Obsidian resources and views.

topics.title: Canvas
topics.summary: Canvas provides a spatial workspace where notes, text cards, media and other resources can be arranged and connected.

topics.title: Bases
topics.summary: Bases provides structured views over notes and their metadata, enabling property-oriented filtering, sorting and collection workflows.

topics.title: File recovery
topics.summary: File Recovery keeps local snapshots that can help recover recently changed or deleted note content. It is not a substitute for an independent backup.

topics.title: Note composer
topics.summary: Note Composer supports refactoring operations that merge note content or extract selected material into another note.
commands: Merge current file with another file

topics.title: Outline
topics.summary: Outline presents the heading hierarchy of the active note as a navigable structural view.

topics.title: Page preview
topics.summary: Page Preview allows linked content to be inspected without permanently navigating away from the current context.

topics.title: Slash commands
topics.summary: Slash Commands exposes command discovery from inside the editor and complements the global Command palette.

topics.title: Slides
topics.summary: Slides provides a presentation-oriented interpretation of Markdown note content.

topics.title: Unique note creator
topics.summary: Unique Note Creator supports creation of notes with uniqueness-oriented names, commonly using time-based conventions.

topics.title: Word count
topics.summary: Word Count exposes word and character-count information for note content.

topics.title: Workspaces
topics.summary: Workspaces save and restore arrangements of Obsidian views and panes for task-specific layouts.

topics.title: Random note
topics.summary: Random Note opens a randomly selected note and can support serendipitous resurfacing and review workflows.

topics.title: Obsidian Sync
topics.summary: Obsidian Sync is the official synchronization service for keeping vault data synchronized across supported devices. Synchronization should not be treated as identical to an independent backup.

topics.title: Obsidian Publish
topics.summary: Obsidian Publish is the official workflow for publishing selected vault content as a website.

topics.title: Community plugins
topics.summary: Community plugins extend Obsidian with third-party code and therefore introduce trust, maintenance and compatibility considerations.

topics.title: CSS snippets
topics.summary: CSS snippets provide targeted visual customization using stylesheet rules stored in the vault configuration area.

examples.purpose: Illustrate a narrowly scoped CSS rule.

topics.title: Obsidian URI
topics.summary: Obsidian URI provides URL-style actions that can open Obsidian and target vaults, notes or supported operations from outside the application.

examples.purpose: Illustrate the general deep-link pattern for opening vault content.

topics.title: Back up your Obsidian files
topics.summary: A resilient Obsidian setup includes an independent backup of vault files in addition to synchronization or short-term recovery mechanisms.

topics.title: Import notes
topics.summary: Obsidian provides migration and import workflows for bringing content from other note-taking systems into a Markdown-oriented vault.

topics.title: Web viewer
topics.summary: Web Viewer is a newer built-in web-content viewing workflow where available; exact behavior and availability are version-sensitive.

steps.action: Choose or create a folder to use as a vault.
Open the folder as an Obsidian vault.
Create an internal link to a note, heading, or block.
Use backlinks or outgoing links to inspect the resulting relationship.
Open or create the daily note for the current date.

limitations.details: The completed research pass did not individually materialize every English Help page, so this single-file artifact must not be treated as a complete mirror.
Newer capabilities such as Bases and Web Viewer may change more quickly than long-standing Markdown and linking behavior.
Synchronization and independent backup address different risks; Sync should not be treated as the only backup mechanism.

retrieval_rules: Prefer exact topic matches before relationship expansion.
Expand related_topics by at most one hop unless the query requires broader context.
Always return source_urls with grounded answers.
Do not turn recommendations or examples into documented product behavior.
For version-sensitive topics, retrieve the current official page before answering version-specific questions.
